idiom_name: Slick TableQuery[Coffees] (+ the plain-SQL interpolator for hand-written statements)
implementation_notes: Slick provides the per-table accessor: a class extending Table[...] with a TableQuery value compiles collection-style operations (coffees.filter(_.price < limit).map(_.name).result) into SQL, executed through db.run(...) as a Future and returning tuples or case classes - the records. Hand-written statements stay first-class via the interpolator sql"select ... where price < $limit".as[Double], which binds parameters and keeps the SQL for a table in one place; Doobie gives the same shape over JDBC with ConnectionIO/Transactor. Prefer TableQuery for CRUD-shaped access and Plain SQL when the statement is tuned by hand or uses features the DSL cannot express.
pitfalls: The generated SQL depends on the profile/dialect; a query tuned on one backend may be planned differently after a driver or profile change.
db.run(...) returns a Future - blocking on it with Await defeats the design and can starve the fixed execution context that the driver shares.
The column definitions and the * projection must stay in sync with the table, or rows map onto the wrong tuple positions with only type errors to catch it.
Slick's artifacts differ between Scala 2 and Scala 3 and by minor version; a mismatched profile version is a runtime failure, not a compile error.
